basic_info.name: Geviti (Geviti Health Inc., gogeviti.com)
basic_info.category: Longevity/health-optimization platform bundling lab testing + AI interpretation + telemedicine clinic + supplement/prescription commerce
basic_info.country: United States (47 states for testing; 29 states for prescription services; excludes AK, HI, RI)
basic_info.stage: Startup/early-growth: founded 2022, $8.5M raised over 1 round [uncertain], small but real traction (450,000+ lab tests run, iOS app v4.x updated Aug 2026)
basic_info.pricing_model: Two tiers. Free: $0, app access only — upload existing lab results, Makor AI insights, retail-priced a-la-carte testing (Longeviti Panel $350) and supplements, no credit card. Plus: $127/mo billed annually at $1,529.99 (or $899/6mo semi-annual per 2025 blog), positioned as 'from $4/day' vs '$10,000+/yr of care'. Includes 100+ biomarker panel 2x/year, at-home draws, Blueprint with specialist video review, quarterly specialist/clinician visits, unlimited Makor AI, Rx catalog (HRT, peptides, GLP-1s), custom supplements at 40% off (Xymogen). Cash-pay only (no insurance/Medicare/Medicaid); HSA/FSA eligible incl. Truemed Letters of Medical Necessity for supplements. No long-term contract; cancel anytime but fees non-refundable for remaining period. Price appears to have risen over time (older Reddit-era mentions of tiers from ~$54/mo) [uncertain].
basic_info.target_user: US health optimizers / biohacker-adjacent consumers 30-60 who can pay ~$1,500/yr cash; influencer-driven audience (Alex Clark, Brett Cooper, Miles Burris, Robbi Jan testimonials); 'complement your regular doctor' positioning
basic_info.scale_metrics: 450,000+ lab tests run (self-reported, homepage); press features (Fox Business, ABC News, Bloomberg, CBS, Yahoo); $8.5M funding over 1 round [uncertain]; Trustpilot 4.0 from only 15-17 reviews; iOS app 4.77 stars from 26 ratings (small volume). Claims 78% of members show clinically meaningful biomarker improvement within 6 months and 93% improvement in >=1 category, 4.9 satisfaction — all self-reported, no published methodology. Durable-threat signal: mid, not noise — real clinical operations and telemedicine infrastructure, but tiny review base and mixed Reddit reports vs Function Health's scale.

product.core_features: Longeviti Panel (100+ biomarkers, 2x/year included in Plus); mobile phlebotomy at-home draws or Quest requisition; AI-generated 'Longevity Blueprint' (video walkthrough of results, nutrition/lifestyle guidance, custom supplement formula); dedicated Longevity Specialist with quarterly visits + async messaging; Makor AI 24/7 chat (free tier too); custom supplement blends via Xymogen (40% member discount); telemedicine prescriptions (HRT, peptides, GLP-1s; no acute care); specialty testing marketplace (gut, genetics); wearable integration (Apple Health, Oura); free-tier lab upload with AI insights.
product.signature_differentiator: The cadence-plus-clinic bundle: the SAME full 100+ biomarker panel every 6 months (Function re-tests only ~60 markers mid-year and drops hormones/thyroid/nutrients), wrapped in an in-house telemedicine loop — specialist video review of each panel, prescriptions written off abnormal results (HRT, peptides), and supplements auto-built from the labs. Marketing thesis is exactly longitudinal: 'a plan that evolves with you', 'retest every six months, your Specialist reviews what's changed, adjusts your protocol'. Second signature: Makor AI (launched 2026) offered free without membership — a first-to-market [uncertain] free clinically-positioned AI lab interpreter that doubles as top-of-funnel for the paid clinic.
product.lab_data_handling: Own-channel-first model: they SELL the blood draw, not just interpret it. Plus members get the Longeviti Panel 2x/year included (panel 'valued at $2,200+' a-la-carte at $350 for free tier); 12h fast, 72h supplement washout; results in 5-10 business days (vs Function's 3-4 weeks). Collection via licensed mobile phlebotomist at home or any Quest Diagnostics location using Geviti's requisition. Uses 'research-based optimal ranges personalized to age and sex — not broad population averages'. Free users can upload existing lab results for Makor AI interpretation. No CGM hardware, no home chip; wearables (Apple Health, Oura) are passive data inputs only.
product.family_dependents_depth: None found. Single-user product; FAQ and site never mention dependents, spouse plans, caregiver mode, pediatric panels or hereditary-risk views — family only appears as marketing lifestyle photography. Both men and women served with the same personalized protocol logic. For Dr. Exame this is an open flank: Geviti (like all US longevity platforms) has zero family/caregiver depth.
product.doctor_sharing: Not a visible feature. FAQ covers nothing about sharing results with your own doctor, exporting/printing records, or generating a consultation brief [uncertain]. Their explicit stance is the opposite of sharing: bring the care IN-HOUSE — 'Geviti is designed to complement your regular care', Geviti providers interpret and prescribe themselves. Post-cancellation only 'your health records remain available to you'. No PDF-export-to-physician or SOAP-style brief is advertised anywhere.
product.action_loop_monetization: Textbook action-loop margin capture: labs -> AI Blueprint -> supplement formula (Xymogen, 40% off but recurring) -> telemedicine prescriptions (peptides, HRT, GLP-1s — 'full Rx catalog access') -> 6-month retest justifies protocol adjustments -> repeat. Peptide medications and specialty diagnostics are purchased separately at member pricing on top of the $1,529 membership. Wholesale pricing on peptides marketed vs standard markups. The free tier is the funnel: upload your labs -> Makor AI insights -> upgrade for specialist + treatment. HSA/FSA paperwork (Truemed) lowers friction. This is the margin model Function Health refuses (data-only) — Geviti monetizes everything downstream of the lab result.

technology.ai_approach: Makor AI — proprietary branding on top of LLM retrieval/decision-support: '5-phase clinical decision-support pipeline that mirrors how top specialists analyze' (data analysis -> protocol validation -> personalized care synthesis), trained on 'thousands of clinical protocols and millions of personalized data combinations', benchmarked against optimal ranges (not population-normal ranges) with 'multi-layer AI guardrails validating every recommendation against evidence-based clinical protocols'. Explicitly marketed as 'not ChatGPT for health', grounded in Geviti's clinical dataset, member outcomes and medical literature. Human-in-loop: Wellness/Longevity Specialist reviews AI recommendations; visit transcripts feed back into the model context. No published accuracy metrics, model cards or peer-reviewed validation.
technology.data_inputs: 100+ blood biomarkers (Longeviti Panel), medical history, active medications, active supplements, daily journals, specialty testing (gut microbiome, genetics), wearable metrics (Apple Health, Oura), visit transcripts, and free-tier uploads of existing lab results.
technology.data_interoperability: Ingestion: manual upload of existing lab results (free tier), own lab channel, Apple Health and Oura wearable sync. No mention of FHIR, Health Connect, Apple Health Records, LIS integration, or structured API access. Exhaust: none advertised — no export format, no doctor-facing API, no WhatsApp (US market). Interoperability is deliberately thin: value stays inside their walled loop (upload data in, buy protocol out).
technology.platform: Web app + iOS app (4.77 stars, 26 ratings, v4.0.11, updated Aug 2026) + Google Play app; Next.js marketing site; Spanish-language site version exists (/es). No public API.

ux.onboarding: Sign up free (no credit card) -> 15-minute health intake questionnaire -> schedule bloodwork (at-home phlebotomist or Quest requisition) -> 12h fast -> results in 5-10 business days -> AI Blueprint with video walkthrough -> meet dedicated Longevity Specialist within 30-45 days. Time-to-first-value: ~2-3 weeks (lab turnaround gates everything), with Makor AI available immediately if uploading existing labs on the free tier.
ux.data_visualization: Results presented 'as a system, not marker by marker' by AI + specialists; Blueprint video walkthrough of results; 6-month retest comparisons drive the 'what changed' narrative; personal benchmarks use age/sex-specific optimal ranges. No evidence of rich trend charts, reference-range banding or health scores in public materials [uncertain] — the visualization centerpiece is the specialist video review, not a charting UI.
ux.engagement_channel: Retention built on human relationships + AI: dedicated named Longevity Specialist (quarterly visits, async messaging anytime), 24/7 Makor AI chat, care-team coordinators, 6-month retest cadence as structural recurrence, daily journals as a lightweight check-in mechanic, custom supplements delivered home (recurring shipments). No community, streaks or group features observed. Channel is the app + SMS/email [uncertain]; nothing WhatsApp-like (US context).

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Weak-to-moderate. Claims are marketing-grade: 78% clinically meaningful improvement / 93% >=1 category / 4.9 satisfaction are self-reported with no published methodology, sample definition or third-party audit; Makor AI accuracy unvalidated publicly. No named medical board or chief medical officer surfaced in any material reviewed [uncertain]. Human review exists (specialist video reviews, physician-supervised peptides) which is more than pure-AI rivals. Independent signal is thin: Trustpilot 4.0 from ~15-17 reviews; Reddit mixed — 'most impressive' in r/Function_Health alternatives thread vs a 'Geviti is AWFUL / worst money I ever spent' annual-subscription complaint. Transparency of billing is decent (HSA/FSA docs, Truemed), but membership fees non-refundable after cancellation.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: US posture: legal-distancing shell identical to Function Health — footer disclaimer states Geviti 'IS A HEALTHCARE TECHNOLOGY COMPANY AND NOT A LABORATORY OR MEDICAL PROVIDER', all lab/medical services rendered by independent third parties, and Geviti 'DOES NOT OFFER MEDICAL ADVICE... DIAGNOSIS, MEDICAL TREATMENT, OR ANY FORM OF MEDICAL OPINION'. Behind the shell: real telemedicine (prescriptions in 29 states vs testing in 47 — the gap maps to state medical-licensing constraints), peptides via licensed compounding pharmacies under physician supervision (aggressive gray zone the FDA has flagged industry-wide), GLP-1s and HRT off lab results. HIPAA compliance, SOC (AICPA) badge, encryption at rest/in transit, 'data never sold'. No FDA SaMD posture needed for a text interpreter; no published clinical validation. Brazilian read: ANVISA RDC 657/2022 would likely classify the full loop (AI interpretation driving prescriptions) far beyond wellness — Geviti's model only works in a cash-pay telehealth regime the CFM/ANVISA environment does not permit.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they DON'T do (Dr. Exame openings): (1) zero family/dependents/caregiver depth — no pediatric ranges, no hereditary-risk view, single-user only; (2) no bring-your-own-exam interpretation as the CORE product — interpretation is bait for their own lab sales; users of random Brazilian labs have nothing to buy; (3) no doctor-collaboration surface — no export, brief or SOAP for YOUR physician; care is captured in-house; (4) no broad ingestion (PDF/FHIR/Health Connect) — thin interoperability by design; (5) price point ($1,529/yr) excludes the mass market; (6) no community/social layer. What WORKS (inspiration, not copy): the 6-month full-panel retest cadence as the product's heartbeat validates the longitudinal-trend thesis; specialist VIDEO review attached to every panel (human-in-loop sells trust AI alone can't); free AI interpreter as top-of-funnel; optimal-vs-normal ranges personalized by age/sex; supplements auto-composed from labs with one-vendor fulfillment (Xymogen); the '$10,000 of care for $4/day' anchor framing.
trust_gaps.relevance: High. Geviti is the purest expression of the exact thesis Dr. Exame is betting on — longitudinal biomaker cadence (2x/year full panel vs Function's 1x + partial) with clinician review of trends — PLUS it proves the action-loop monetization model (supplements + telemedicine Rx) that Function refuses. In Brazil it cannot replicate (cash-pay telemedicine + peptide/HRT prescribing is not legally available), so it is a model to learn from rather than a direct entrant; its absence of family depth, BYO-exam interpretation and doctor-sharing are precisely Dr. Exame's differentiating pillars.
